text:
maria: Heads up - spotted a ~3-6% p99 latency bump on prod during KV-cache sampling runs overnight. I ran a short nsys trace and a PMU-sampled run, attaching quick notes below. Anyone seen similar?

ajay: curious, is that when the sampler enabled full-stack unwinds or just instruction sampling?

maria: It was two tests: (1) nsys full timeline for 30s, kernel+cuda stacks, (2) perf record -F 99 with callchains for the same workload.

maria: nsys output looked like ~110ms extra GPU gap time because of the tracer hooking into cudaLaunch paths. perf sampling added ~1.8% CPU across workers. aggregate ~= 3.5% extra for tail.

devon: can you paste the exact commands you used?

maria: sure: 
```
# nsys full timeline (dev box)
nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,cudaRuntime -o /tmp/trace nsys_target -- ./bench --batch-size=8 --iters=300
# perf sampling (system-wide)
perf record -F 99 -g -a -- sleep 30
perf script > /tmp/perf.stacks
```

maria: short excerpt from nsys summary: 
```
GPU Activity Idle Time: +112ms (during sampling windows)
API Overhead: cudaLaunch overhead increased by ~45us/op sampled
```

ajay: interesting. my hypothesis: the full timeline adds instrumentation that forces kernel serialization for our small kernels, especially when we do kernel selection switching. That could explain per-op overhead.

sophie: do we have a budget/guardrail for in-prod traces? e.g., only sample 1 request / 10k or run full trace only during canaries?

maria: we don't currently. I prototyped a budgeted policy: if cluster p99 latency delta > 5% abort full trace; else limit full traces to 0.1% of requests and use in-process lightweight counters for hot-path detection.

devon: +1 on budgeted full traces. Also consider a two-stage approach: lightweight PMU sampling continuously (low overhead, callstack-limited) and only trigger nsys full timeline for 1 trace after we detect a consistent spike.
ajay: that fits with kernel selection debugging: swapping kernels for short sequences can cause micro-serialization, which nsys amplifies. Detect with PMU & perf events (branch-misses, dTLB) and only then do the expensive timeline.
maria: I also observed the KV-cache sampler (we sample prefix cache hits at 5%) introduces lock contention on the cache stats object when many concurrent requests hit the same shard. That produced CPU-side tail and made the relative overhead of the tracer look worse.
sophie: Can you repro with a microbench? If it's the shard lock we can switch to per-thread counters + merge or sharded atomics to avoid global contention.
maria: repro script attached gist-ish snippet: 
```
# microbench to stress KV sampler
for i in {1..1000}; do ./kv_hit_sim --threads=128 --hot-key=42 & done; wait
# with sampler on: sample_rate=0.05 -> latency tail + mutex contention
```

devon: small patch idea: move sampling bookkeeping to per-core ring buffer and flush in background. Should drop the sampling critical section to near-zero.
ajay: also add a tracer whitelist: on prod only allow timeline traces for routes marked `debug=yes` and require canary window. Any full-timeline must be signed off or auto-killed if latency delta crosses threshold.
sophie: agree. We should also provide an admin API to query current trace budget consumed per-customer so SRE can throttle.
maria: action items: (1) devon to prototyped per-core ring-buffer sampler (2) ajay to add budgeted-trace policy + whitelist in routing layer (3) maría to run a controlled A/B comparing perf sampling vs nsys overhead on a per-kernel basis and post numbers. I'll post the perf/nvprof artifacts in shared drive.
devon: I'll send a quick draft PR for ring-buffer sampler today. Expect microbench numbers in thread.
ajay: I'll sketch the budget policy and a small state machine: START->LIGHT_SAMPLING->ELEVATE->FULL_TRACE (with thresholds) and put it behind a feature flag.
sophie: I'll add the tracer-budget dashboard in Console to show current consumption and recent kill events.
maria: thanks all. TL;DR: sampling is safe at low rates, full timeline can induce kernel serialization and worsen tails; guardrail with budget + light sampling + sharded counters should mitigate. tagging perf-bot for nightly regression alert tuning. :rocket:

perf-bot: scheduled ci/regression-checker job to run 30s perf sampling nightly and emit diffs to #eng-runtime/regressions.
